bibliographic.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI): Concepts, Taxonomies, Opportunities and Challenges toward Responsible AI
bibliographic.authors: Alejandro Barredo Arrieta, Natalia Díaz-Rodríguez, Javier Del Ser, Adrien Bennetot, Siham Tabik, Alberto Barbadó, Salvador García, Sergio Gil-López, Daniel Molina, Richard Benjamins, Raja Chatila, Francisco Herrera

bibliographic.citation_apa: Barredo Arrieta, A., Díaz-Rodríguez, N., Del Ser, J., Bennetot, A., Tabik, S., Barbadó, A., García, S., Gil-López, S., Molina, D., Benjamins, R., Chatila, R., & Herrera, F. methodology.method_family: critical literature analysis with taxonomy development
methodology.study_design: narrative literature review proposing definitions and dual taxonomies for XAI methods in ML and Deep Learning
methodology.sample_description: existing literature and contributions in the field of XAI
methodology.sector: general AI and Machine Learning across multiple application sectors
methodology.technology_context: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Deep Neural Networks, explainable AI methods, data fusion

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper is a 2019 pre-LLM literature review and taxonomy on XAI and Responsible AI covering ML and Deep Learning explainability, accountability, fairness, and transparency. It does not address LLM-based conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance in regulated environments, but provides foundational conceptual framing relevant to governance dimensions such as explainability and accountability.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted Python metadata incorrectly parsed author affiliations as title; full-text beyond provided excerpts was not supplied for verification of regulated-domain mentions and review methodology.

appraisal.notes: Clear objectives and structured taxonomies are described, but provided excerpts do not document systematic search, inclusion criteria, or corpus size. Strong as conceptual synthesis; limited direct applicability to LLM conversational governance without extrapolation.

cerqual.explanation: The review presents a coherent XAI taxonomy and Responsible AI prospect with explicit governance-related concepts, but methodological transparency and sampling are unclear from the supplied text, and topical relevance to LLM conversational governance in regulated settings is indirect.

coding.theme: Explainable AI foundations toward Responsible AI
coding.subtheme: Taxonomies of explainability methods for ML and Deep Learning

synthesis.main_claim: Explainability is a crucial barrier and enabler for practical AI deployment in ML; the authors define explainable ML, propose taxonomies of XAI contributions including a Deep Learning-specific taxonomy, identify remaining XAI challenges, and prospect toward Responsible AI with fairness, explainability, and accountability at its core.
synthesis.contribution: Foundational conceptual synthesis, definitions, and taxonomic organization of XAI literature to support future research and organizational adoption of responsible AI.
synthesis.limitations: Predates LLMs; focuses on ML/DNN explainability rather than conversational systems; review search and selection procedures are not evidenced in the supplied excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as foundational contextual evidence for explainability, transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy, and Responsible AI concepts that may inform conversational governance frameworks, but not as central empirical or LLM-specific evidence.
